items.followUp: Draw the truth table for “P OR Q.”

rubric.why: A truth table must show all four possible input combinations.
rubric.description: Lists all possible combinations of P and Q.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark if all four input combinations are shown.

rubric.why: P AND Q is true only when both inputs are true.
rubric.description: Gives the correct output for each input combination.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark if all four outputs are correct.

rubric.why: Sabotage is a deliberate rather than accidental act.
rubric.description: States that sabotage is deliberate or intentional.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying sabotage as deliberate or intentional.

rubric.why: Sabotage harms a computer system or interferes with its normal operation.
rubric.description: Identifies damage to a computer system or disruption of its operation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the damage or disruption.

modelAnswer: Sabotage is the deliberate act of damaging a computer system, its data or network, or disrupting its normal operation.

rubric.why: Cipher text is produced by encrypting an original message.
rubric.description: Identifies cipher text as an encrypted or enciphered message.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as encrypted or enciphered text.

rubric.why: The original message becomes understandable after decryption using the appropriate key.
rubric.description: Explains that the cipher text must be decrypted using a key to be understood.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining the need for decryption with a key.

modelAnswer: Cipher text is the encrypted form of an original message (plain text).
It is not normally understandable until it is decrypted using the appropriate key.

rubric.why: A network of networks is formed by linking multiple computer networks.
rubric.description: States that multiple networks are interconnected.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing networks as interconnected.

rubric.why: The Internet is a common example of a network of networks.
rubric.description: Names the Internet as an example.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the Internet.

modelAnswer: A network of networks is a system formed by interconnecting many computer networks.
The Internet is the largest example of a network of networks.

items.followUp: Are HTML tag names case-sensitive? Give an example.

rubric.why: HTML treats uppercase and lowercase tag names alike.
rubric.description: States that HTML is not case-sensitive.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that HTML is not case-sensitive.

rubric.why: The example shows that differently cased forms of the same tag are treated alike.
rubric.description: Gives a correct example of equivalent uppercase and lowercase tags.
rubric.how:
Award 1 mark for a correct example such as

and

.

modelAnswer: HTML is not case sensitive, so uppercase and lowercase letters in tag names are treated alike.

For example,

and

represent the same paragraph tag. Lowercase tags are generally preferred.
